mainTopic: The laws of תפילין straps and knots, and when to say the ברכה
overview: This amud gives a practical guide to תפילין straps and knots. It opens with a second way to tell 'new' תפילין from 'old' ones. Then it rules that a torn רצועה may not be knotted, because וקשרתם means a complete binding. For sewing with hidden stitches, רב אשי says to follow common practice. רב פפא's view that leftover strap pieces are kosher is rejected: תכלת and אזוב are only תשמישי מצוה, but תפילין are תשמישי קדושה. So straps must have a minimum length, measured up to the index finger. The גמרא then teaches that the תפילין knot is a הלכה למשה מסיני. Its nice side must face outward, and it must sit high and toward the front. Two פסוקים are linked to the head תפילין and to the knot that ה׳ showed משה. Finally, the ברכה on תפילין is said after putting them on but before tying them, so it still comes before the מצוה.

steps.title: A second way to define new and old תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another test for which תפילין count as 'new' and which as 'old'. If the box stays on when you hang it by the strap, it is new. If not, it is old.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: whenever you hang the תפילין by the strap and the box follows along with it, they are 'new'. In the other case they are 'old'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier discussion that distinguished 'new' תפילין from 'old' ones. Here it gives a second, alternative definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is practical. Lift the תפילין by the strap. If the box stays firmly attached and comes along, the strap and box are still tight, so they count as 'new'. If the box would slip off, they count as 'old'.

phrases.english: Alternatively, in any case
where, when one hangs it by the strap,
it comes along after it,
phrases.notes: The 'it' that comes along is the box of the תפילין. It stays attached when you lift the strap.

phrases.english: those are new; and the other – old.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי נָמֵי כֹּל הֵיכִי דְּכִי מִיתְּלֵי בֵּיהּ בְּמִתְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second definition, continuing a discussion from the previous section
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: New תפילין are those whose box stays on when hung by the strap. Old ones are those where it does not.

steps.title: אביי asks about knotting a torn strap
steps.stepSummary: While sitting before רב יוסף, אביי's תפילין strap tears. He asks whether he may tie it back together.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי was sitting before רב יוסף, and the strap of his תפילין tore. He said to him: What is the law about tying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that opens a new topic: repairing a torn תפילין strap. אביי asks a practical question, and רב יוסף answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether a knot joining the two torn pieces is good enough for a kosher רצועה. Or does the strap need to be one whole piece?

keyTerms.meaning: The leather strap of the תפילין

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: Abaye was sitting before Rav Yosef,
the strap of his tefillin tore;
he said to him: What is the law about tying it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about repairing straps
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May a torn תפילין strap be repaired by tying a knot?

steps.title: No knots, because the binding must be complete
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers from the פסוק 'וקשרתם' that the binding must be a complete, whole binding. So a knotted torn strap is not acceptable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is written 'And you shall bind them', meaning the binding must be complete.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי's question with a פסוק. You may not just knot the strap back together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וקשרתם is read as 'a complete binding' (קשירה תמה). A strap patched together with a makeshift knot is not a whole, proper binding.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall bind them' (the פסוק about תפילין)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule that a torn strap cannot simply be knotted. That leads straight into the next question about sewing.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is written 'And you shall bind them,'
that the binding should be complete.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״וּקְשַׁרְתָּם״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No; the פסוק requires a complete binding, so a knotted strap is not acceptable.

steps.title: Sewing the strap with hidden stitches
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב יוסף asks רב אשי whether a torn strap may be sewn, with the stitching turned inward so it is not seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רב יוסף, said to רב אשי: What is the law about sewing it and putting the stitching inside?
steps.whatsHappening: Knotting is ruled out. Now a new question is asked: what about sewing the strap with the stitches hidden on the inside? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hidden stitches might make the strap look whole from the outside. That could perhaps satisfy the need for a 'complete binding' in a way a knot does not.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Yosef, said to Rav Ashi:
What is the law about sewing it
and putting the stitching inside?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לְרַב אָשֵׁי: מַהוּ לְמִיתְפְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up the ban on knotting by asking about a different repair method
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May a torn strap be sewn with the stitching hidden inside?

steps.title: Go see what people do
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the matter depends on common practice. Go out and see what people are doing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Go out and see what the people are doing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי does not give a direct yes or no. He sends the questioner to look at the accepted custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a law is unclear, the common practice of the people can decide it. If people commonly sew straps this way, it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out and see what the people are doing; follow common practice

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: פּוֹק חֲזִי מָה עַמָּא דָּבַר.
phrases.english: He said: Go out and see what the people are doing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: פּוֹק חֲזִי מָה עַמָּא דָּבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Follow the common custom; if people do it, it is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Knotting a torn strap is not allowed (וקשרתם means a complete binding). Sewing with hidden stitches depends on common practice.

steps.title: רב פפא: leftover strap pieces are kosher
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that גרדומי רצועות, what is left of a strap after part was cut off, are still kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: Leftover remnants of straps are kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא states a new ruling: a strap that got shortened can still be used. The גמרא will challenge this next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a strap does not lose its status just because part of it was cut off. Whatever is left still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Remnants; leftover pieces after part was cut off

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
Remnants of straps are fit,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: גַּרְדּוּמֵּי רְצוּעוֹת כְּשֵׁירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New statement about straps, related to the repair topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shortened leftover pieces of תפילין straps remain kosher.

steps.title: Rejected: בני רבי חייא listed only תכלת and אזוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב פפא's ruling is incorrect. בני רבי חייא listed remnants of תכלת and אזוב as kosher, and they did not include straps.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so, since the sons of רבי חייא say: remnants of תכלת and remnants of אזוב are kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב פפא's ruling. It shows that בני רבי חייא made a list of kosher remnants, and straps were not on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from what is left out. If strap remnants were also kosher, בני רבי חייא would have listed them alongside תכלת and אזוב.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is not correct; a rejection formula
Hyssop, used for sprinkling the פרה אדומה water

steps.confusionAlert: בני רבי חייא never directly mention straps. The rejection comes from the fact that straps are missing from their list, not from an explicit statement about them.

phrases.english: But that is not so,
as can be seen from what the sons of Rabbi Ḥiyya say:
Remnants of sky-blue wool
and remnants of hyssop are fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא, מִדְּאָמְרִי בְּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's ruling
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of רב פפא's ruling that strap remnants are kosher
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: בני רבי חייא listed only תכלת and אזוב remnants as kosher, which implies strap remnants are not.

steps.title: Why straps are stricter: holiness versus מצוה use
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the difference. תכלת and אזוב are תשמישי מצוה, items used for a מצוה‎. תפילין straps are תשמישי קדושה, items of holiness, so their remnants are not kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, remnants are kosher because they are items used for a מצוה. But here, they are items of holiness, so no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why בני רבי חייא left straps off their list. This finishes the rejection of רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תכלת and אזוב are only tools used to do a מצוה‎. תפילין straps belong to a holy object, so they are held to a higher standard. A shortened strap therefore does not stay kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Items used to perform a מצוה (lower level)
Items serving something holy (higher level), like תפילין

steps.whatToRemember: Remnants of תכלת and אזוב are kosher because they are תשמישי מצוה. Remnants of תפילין straps are not kosher, because they are תשמישי קדושה and held to a higher standard.
steps.whyThisMatters: The split between תשמישי מצוה and תשמישי קדושה is a basic rule that comes up across many areas of הלכה.

phrases.english: It is there that they are fit, since they are articles of a מצוה;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּתַשְׁמִישֵׁי קְדוּשָּׁה נִינְהוּ – לָא.
phrases.english: but here, since they are articles of sanctity – no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם הוּא דְּתַשְׁמִישֵׁי מִצְוָה נִינְהוּ, אֲבָל הָכָא דְּתַשְׁמִישֵׁי קְדוּשָּׁה נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the rejection in step 7
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Leftover pieces of תפילין straps are not kosher, because תפילין are תשמישי קדושה, unlike תכלת and אזוב, which are תשמישי מצוה.

steps.title: Straps must have a minimum length, so how long?
steps.stepSummary: From the discussion about strap leftovers, the גמרא infers that straps have a set minimum length, and asks what it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: This shows that the straps have a minimum measure. So how long is that measure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the last discussion and then asks a new question: how long must the straps be? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If leftovers of a strap can be too short to use, then there must be a required length. So the גמרא now asks for that exact שיעור.

keyTerms.meaning: by inference; from this we can conclude
a set measure or minimum size

phrases.english: By inference, they have a minimum measure,
phrases.notes: "They" means the תפילין straps. Talking about leftovers being too short only makes sense if straps have a set length.

phrases.english: and how much is their measure?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּאִית לְהוּ שִׁיעוּרָא, וְכַמָּה שִׁיעוּרַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ruling that strap remnants are not kosher, which implies a minimum length.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum required length of תפילין straps.

steps.title: The measure: up to the index finger
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא, quoting ריש לקיש, gives the measure of the straps: up to the index finger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said in the name of ריש לקיש: the measure is up to the index finger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a measure based on the hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer gives a hand measure, but it does not yet say exactly how to hold the hand. That detail comes in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said that Reish Lakish said:
Up to the index finger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ עַד אֶצְבַּע צְרֵדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The strap length is measured up to the index finger.

steps.title: Two ways of showing the measure
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא showed the measure with a bent hand, and רב אשי showed it with a straight hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא would show it bent. רב אשי would show it straight.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים show in practice how to measure "up to the index finger."
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא measured with the fingers spread, from the tip of the middle finger to the tip of the index finger. רב אשי measured from the tip of the thumb to the tip of the index finger, which is longer.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana would demonstrate it bent,
phrases.notes: With the fingers spread, measuring from the tip of the middle finger to the tip of the index finger.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi would demonstrate it straight.
phrases.notes: Measuring from the tip of the thumb to the tip of the index finger, fingers spread.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא מַחְוֵי כָּפוּף, רַב אָשֵׁי מַחְוֵי פָּשׁוּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how to apply the measure given in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The index-finger measure is shown either with a bent hand (רב כהנא) or a straight hand (רב אשי).
steps.whatToRemember: Straps have a minimum length, measured up to the index finger. רב כהנא and רב אשי showed two different ways to measure it.

steps.title: How different sages wore their straps
steps.stepSummary: רבה tied the straps and let them hang behind him. רב אחא בר יעקב tied and braided them. מר בריה דרבנא did as we do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה would tie them, release them, and let them fall behind him. רב אחא בר יעקב would tie them and braid them. מר בריה דרבנא did like we do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports three different customs for what to do with the straps after tying them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No ruling is given here. The גמרא simply records the practice of each אמורא, and "like we do" means letting the straps hang down in front.

keyTerms.meaning: like ours, the way we do it

phrases.english: Rabba would tie them
and release them and let them fall,
phrases.notes: He let the straps fall behind his back.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב קָטַר לְהוּ
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov would tie them
and braid them,
Mar, son of Ravna, would do like us.
phrases.notes: He let the straps hang down over the front of his body.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה קָטַר לְהוּ וּפָשֵׁיט וְשָׁדֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the strap length to how the straps were worn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three practices for the straps: hanging behind, braided, or hanging in front.

steps.title: The תפילין knot is from סיני
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, teaches that the knot of תפילין is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה son of רב שמואל בר שילת said in the name of רב: the knot of תפילין is a law given to משה at סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching: the shape of the תפילין knot comes from a tradition handed to משה at סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The knot is not just a practical way to hold the תפילין on. Its form is a הלכה למשה מסיני, meaning an oral law with no פסוק behind it. The knot makes the shape of a letter: a ד on the head and a י on the arm.

keyTerms.meaning: a law taught orally to משה at סיני

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said in the name of Rav:
The knot of tefillin
phrases.notes: This means the knot shaped like a letter: ד on the head, י on the arm.

phrases.english: is a law given to Moshe at Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: קֶשֶׁר שֶׁל תְּפִילִּין הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from wearing the straps to the knot itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The form of the תפילין knot is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the required ד and י shapes of the knots.

steps.title: The nice side faces outward
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן adds that the nice side of the knot must face out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: and their nice side must face outward.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds a detail to the rule about the knot: its good-looking side must face out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "nice side" is the black side, where the letter shape can be seen. It must be visible from the outside, not turned toward the body.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: And their decorative side faces outward.
phrases.notes: The nice side is the black side, where the letter shape shows.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן וְנוֹיֵיהֶן לְבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to the knot law of step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The decorative (black) side of the knot and straps must face outward.

steps.title: מר זוטרא notices רב אשי's flipped strap
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי's strap flipped over, and מר זוטרא asked him whether he does not hold that the nice side must face out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי was sitting before מר זוטרא, and his תפילין strap got turned over. מר זוטרא said to him: Doesn't the master hold that the nice side faces outward?
steps.whatsHappening: A story: מר זוטרא sees רב אשי's strap turned the wrong way and challenges him with רב נחמן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not really asking for information. It points out that רב אשי seems to be acting against the rule of ונוייהן לבר.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּמָר זוּטְרָא,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi was sitting before Mar Zutra,
and his tefillin strap got turned over.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
phrases.english: He said to him: Doesn't the Master hold
"and their decorative side faces outward"?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר וְנוֹיֵיהֶן לְבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רב נחמן's rule through a story.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the nice side must face out, a flipped strap goes against the rule.

steps.title: רב אשי: I did not notice
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that he simply had not noticed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It was not on my mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains that he does not disagree with the rule; he just did not realize the strap had flipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the rule of ונוייהן לבר in place. The problem was an accident, not a different opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: it wasn't on my mind; I didn't notice

phrases.english: He said to him: It was not on my mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לָאו אַדַּעְתַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר זוטרא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual explanation: it was an accident, not a disagreement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אשי might not hold of ונוייהן לבר.
steps.terutzMaskana: He agrees with the rule; he just did not notice the strap flipped.
steps.whatToRemember: The knot of תפילין is a הלכה למשה מסיני, and its nice black side must face outward. Even רב אשי agreed; his strap had just flipped by accident.

steps.title: The nations will see ה׳'s name: the head תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר הגדול teaches that the פסוק about the nations seeing ה׳'s name on us refers to the head תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And all the nations of the earth shall see that the name of ה׳ is called upon you, and they shall fear you." A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר הגדול says: these are the תפילין on the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads a פסוק in דברים as a hint to the head תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The head תפילין carry ה׳'s name and are seen by everyone. So they are the visible sign that "the name of ה׳ is called upon you."

keyTerms.meaning: the name of ה׳ is called upon you

phrases.english: "And all the nations of the earth shall see
that the name of ה׳ is called upon you
and they shall fear you",
It is taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
These are the tefillin on the head.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָאוּ כׇּל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ כִּי שֵׁם ה׳ נִקְרָא עָלֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to aggadic teachings about תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק "the name of ה׳ is called upon you" refers to the head תפילין.

steps.title: ה׳ showed משה the knot of תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון חסידא reads "you will see My back" as teaching that הקדוש ברוך הוא showed משה the knot of תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And I will remove My hand, and you will see My back." רב חנא בר ביזנא said in the name of רבי שמעון חסידא: this teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא showed משה the knot of תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק, from שמות, and reads it as ה׳ showing משה the תפילין knot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "My back" is read as the back of the head, where the head-תפילין knot sits. This ties back to step 13: the knot is a tradition that משה received directly from ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: the Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: "And I will remove My hand
and you will see My back",

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר בִּיזְנָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן חֲסִידָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chana bar Bizna said that Rabbi Shimon Chasida said:

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהֶרְאָה לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed
Moshe the knot of tefillin.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲסִרֹתִי אֶת כַּפִּי וְרָאִיתָ אֶת אֲחֹרָי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second פסוק about תפילין, connecting back to the knot.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "You will see My back" teaches that ה׳ showed משה the knot of תפילין.
steps.whatToRemember: Two פסוקים are linked to תפילין: the nations seeing ה׳'s name refers to the head תפילין, and "you will see My back" means ה׳ showed משה the knot.

steps.title: The knot must be high and toward the front
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה teaches that the תפילין knot must sit high and face the front, so that ישראל will be on top and in front.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says: The knot of the תפילין must be up high, so that ישראל will be on top and not on the bottom. It must also face the front, so that ישראל will be in front and not behind.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives two rules about where the תפילין knot sits. Each rule comes with a reason that is a sign for כלל ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rule one: the knot must be high, on the head and not slipping down. Rule two: the knot must be toward the front. Each placement stands for ישראל being on top and in front, not below or behind.

keyTerms.meaning: Knot (here, the knot of the head תפילין strap)

steps.whatToRemember: The תפילין knot must be high and toward the front. It is a sign that ישראל should be on top and in front.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: קֶשֶׁר שֶׁל תְּפִילִּין צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּהֵא לְמַעְלָה,
phrases.english: The knot of tefillin must be up high,
phrases.notes: He means up on the head, not slipping down onto the neck.

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַעְלָה וְלֹא לְמַטָּה,
phrases.english: so that Israel will be on top and not on the bottom,
and it must be toward the front,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְפָנִים וְלֹא לְאָחוֹר.
phrases.english: so that Israel will be in front and not behind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: קֶשֶׁר שֶׁל תְּפִילִּין צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּהֵא לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more rules about the תפילין knot, continuing the knot theme from steps 14 and 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The knot of the head תפילין must be placed high and toward the front, as a sign that ישראל should be on top and in front.

steps.title: The ברכה on תפילין is said from when you put them on
steps.stepSummary: A statement with three possible chains of transmission says that the ברכה on תפילין is said from the time you put them on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר בידרי says in the name of רב (and some say רבי אחא אריכא in the name of רב הונא, and some say רב מנשיא in the name of שמואל): When do you make the ברכה on תפילין? From the time you put them on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the timing of the ברכה on תפילין. The answer given is "from the time you put them on."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is not sure who first said this teaching, so it lists three chains of names. The ruling itself is simple: the ברכה is connected to the moment of putting on the תפילין. That wording will soon cause a problem.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר בֵּידָרֵי אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Bideri says that Rav says,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא אֲרִיכָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Acha Arikha says that Rav Huna says,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Menashya says that Shmuel says:
Tefillin, from when does one make the bracha over them?
From the time he puts them on.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּפִילִּין מֵאֵימָתַי מְבָרֵךְ עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the timing of the ברכה on תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה on תפילין is said from the time of putting them on.

steps.title: Every ברכה must come before doing the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the previous step using שמואל's rule that every ברכה on a מצוה must be said before doing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that true? But רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: For all the מצוות, you make the ברכה before doing them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling from step 20. It uses a general rule that every ברכה comes before the מצוה is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "From the time you put them on" sounds like the ברכה comes after the תפילין are already on. But the rule of עובר לעשייתן says the ברכה must come before doing the מצוה. So the two teachings seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Before doing them; the ברכה comes first
All the מצוות, every one of them

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say that Shmuel says:
All the מצוות, every one of them,
one makes the bracha over them before doing them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the ברכה on תפילין is said from the time of putting them on.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every ברכה must come before the מצוה, saying the ברכה after the תפילין are already on seems to be too late.

steps.title: Say the ברכה between putting on and tying
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא explain that the ברכה is said after putting on the תפילין but before tying them, so it still comes before the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both say: From the time of putting them on until the time of tying them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא answer the challenge. They show that the ruling in step 20 and the rule of עובר לעשייתן do not clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting on the תפילין is not yet the complete מצוה. The tying finishes it. So if the ברכה is said after placing the תפילין but before tying them, it still comes before the מצוה is done.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברכה on תפילין goes in the window between putting them on and tying them. The tying counts as doing the מצוה, so the ברכה still comes first.
steps.confusionAlert: "From the time you put them on" does not mean after the מצוה is done. Before the tying, the מצוה is not yet complete.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the rule of עובר לעשייתן works in practice: you need to know exactly which action counts as doing the מצוה.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava both say:
From the time of putting them on
until the time of tying.
phrases.notes: The tying is the real doing of the מצוה, so a ברכה said before it still comes first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining which action is the actual doing of the מצוה (the tying, not the placing).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying the ברכה "from the time of putting on" seemed to mean after the מצוה was already done.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברכה is said between putting on and tying. Since tying is the doing of the מצוה, the ברכה still comes before it.
